question.problem:
For $x,y,z\in {R}^{2},$ consider the following functions: 

$$
\begin{aligned} & y(x)=Ax\,\text{where}\,A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & z(y)=[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}{y}_{2} \\ {y}_{1}-{y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & f(z)=Cz\,\text{where}\,C=[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

What is $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}f(z(y(x)))$ evaluated at ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]?$
question.worked_solution:
Using the chain rule, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}f(z(y(x)))=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}z}\cdot \frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let's consider each of the factors in turn.

- The function $f$ acts on a vector $z\in {R}^{2}$ by multiplying it by $C$ and outputs a vector $f(z)\in {R}^{2}.$ Thus,

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}z}=C.
$$

- The function $z$ acts on a vector $y\in {R}^{2}$ and outputs a vector $z(y)\in {R}^{2}.$ Thus,

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}y}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{z}_{1}}{∂{y}_{1}} & \frac{∂{z}_{1}}{∂{y}_{2}} \\ \frac{∂{z}_{2}}{∂{y}_{1}} & \frac{∂{z}_{2}}{∂{y}_{2}}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}{y}_{2} & {y}_{1} \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Evaluating at ${y}_{0}=A{x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -6\end{aligned}],$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}y}{|}_{{y}_{0}}=[\begin{aligned}-6 & 8 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

- The function $y$ acts on a vector $x\in {R}^{2}$ by multiplying it by $A$ and outputs a vector $y(x)\in {R}^{2}.$ Thus,

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=A.
$$

Therefore, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}f(z(y(x))){|}_{{x}_{0}} & =\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}z}{|}_{{z}_{0}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}y}{|}_{{y}_{0}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{{x}_{0}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-6 & 8 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-19 & 25 \\ 9 & -11\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}19 & -88 \\ -9 & 40\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
